rules: Nominal owner identity and schema identity are resolved compiler symbols, not source spelling or runtime reflection.
Context values evaluate once in source order, then map to declaration slots. Invocation reuses the capture.
Scalar slots can copy; allocator slots cannot be implicitly copied by this model. Allocator identity, owner, generation and region proof must be resolved by backend.
A context containing a borrow cannot escape the lexical lifetime or transfer across actors. This reference model does not issue, validate or revoke actual allocator authority.
Copy or move operations cannot re-evaluate capture expressions. Optimizations must preserve failure, effects, quota and lifetime observations.
Direct primitive construction and user-defined contextual new/make members are distinct until the compiler proves equivalence.

Reference model requires explicit region identity path prefix, not numeric depth. Production must prove region identity and current generation using resolved compiler/runtime authority; symbolic input is not that proof.

Ordered invocation plan separates source-order operand evaluation from declaration-order parameter references. Direct context expressions execute before ordinary arguments; stored invocation references captured slots without recapture.
Resolve schema identity and exact typed slot shape before generating an invocation; duplicate JSON keys, duplicate symbolic operand occurrence IDs and forged extra fields are denied.
limitations: Reference schema and symbolic transfer/lifetime admission only.
No runtime handle, borrow checker, compiler integration, construction, allocation or guest execution proof.

Operand IDs and schema identities in the host reference model are symbolic; production typed IR verification, runtime capability authentication, alias analysis and actual evaluation order remain backend obligations.
